Refuse a declared event level that nothing in the outcome carries

Source: R/decision_curve.R
mm_check_positive.Rd

mm_event_indicator() takes a declared positive_class on trust, which is right for everything mm_project() validates: a project given a cohort refuses a level the outcome does not carry at plan time, so by the time the indicator is built the level is known to exist.

Usage

mm_check_positive(values, positive, caller)

Arguments

values

The outcome column.

positive

The declared event level, or NULL.

caller

The function to name in the message.

Value

TRUE, invisibly, or an error.

Details

The recalibration and decision-curve functions take an outcome and a positive with no project between them, so nothing has checked it. Without this, naming a level that does not exist returns an indicator of all zeros, and the caller is then told their outcome has one class. That is true and it is not the problem: which value was expected should be named. It cannot tell a misnamed level from a sample that genuinely carries no events, so it reports what the outcome does hold and says both readings are open. The same mistake, an unrecognised level quietly becoming something else, was finding W-3 in the calculator.
